GOVERN.name: Govern
GOVERN.description: A culture of risk management is cultivated and present.

subcategories.GOVERN-1.1: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
subcategories.GOVERN-1.2: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, and procedures.
subcategories.GOVERN-1.3: Processes and procedures are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization's risk tolerance.
subcategories.GOVERN-1.4: The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.
subcategories.GOVERN-1.5: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned.
subcategories.GOVERN-1.6: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
subcategories.GOVERN-1.7: Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely.
subcategories.GOVERN-2.1: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented.
subcategories.GOVERN-2.2: The organization's personnel and partners receive AI risk management training.
subcategories.GOVERN-2.3: Executive leadership of the organization takes responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.
subcategories.GOVERN-3.1: Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team.
subcategories.GOVERN-3.2: Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations.
subcategories.GOVERN-4.1: Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset.
subcategories.GOVERN-4.2: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design.
subcategories.GOVERN-4.3: Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.
subcategories.GOVERN-5.1: Organizational policies and practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team.
subcategories.GOVERN-5.2: Mechanisms are established to enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback.
subcategories.GOVERN-6.1: Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities.
subcategories.GOVERN-6.2: Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems.

MAP.name: Map
MAP.description: Context is recognized and risks related to context are identified.

subcategories.MAP-1.1: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms, and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented.
subcategories.MAP-1.2: Interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise.
subcategories.MAP-1.3: The organization's mission and relevant goals for AI technology are understood and documented.
subcategories.MAP-1.4: The business value or context of business use has been clearly defined.
subcategories.MAP-1.5: Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.
subcategories.MAP-1.6: System requirements are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors.
subcategories.MAP-2.1: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined.
subcategories.MAP-2.2: Information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented.
subcategories.MAP-2.3: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented.
subcategories.MAP-3.1: Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.
subcategories.MAP-3.2: Potential costs of the AI system are examined and documented, including non-monetary costs.
subcategories.MAP-3.3: Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system's capability.
subcategories.MAP-3.4: Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness are defined.
subcategories.MAP-3.5: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies.
subcategories.MAP-4.1: Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components are documented.
subcategories.MAP-4.2: Internal risk controls for components of the AI system, including third-party AI technologies, are identified and documented.
subcategories.MAP-5.1: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact based on expected use are identified and documented.
subcategories.MAP-5.2: Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts are in place and documented.

MEASURE.name: Measure
MEASURE.description: Identified risks are assessed, analyzed, or tracked.

subcategories.MEASURE-1.1: Approaches and metrics for measurement of AI risks enumerated during the Map function are selected for implementation.
subcategories.MEASURE-1.2: Appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls is regularly assessed and updated.
subcategories.MEASURE-1.3: Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors are involved in regular assessments and updates.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.1: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV are documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.2: Evaluations involving human subjects meet applicable requirements and are representative of the relevant population.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.3: AI system performance or assurance criteria are measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s).
subcategories.MEASURE-2.4: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components are monitored after deployment.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.5: The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be valid and reliable.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.6: AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.7: AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.8: Risks associated with transparency and accountability are examined and documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.9: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.10: Privacy risk of the AI system is examined and documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.11: Fairness and bias of the AI system is evaluated and results are documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.12: Environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities are assessed and documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-2.13: Effectiveness of the employed TEVV metrics and processes is evaluated and documented.
subcategories.MEASURE-3.1: Approaches, personnel, and documentation are in place to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks.
subcategories.MEASURE-3.2: Risk tracking approaches are considered for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques.
subcategories.MEASURE-3.3: Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems and appeal system outcomes are established and integrated.
subcategories.MEASURE-4.1: Measurement approaches for identifying AI risks are connected to deployment context(s).
subcategories.MEASURE-4.2: Measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context(s) are informed by input from domain experts and relevant AI actors.
subcategories.MEASURE-4.3: Measurable performance improvements based on consultations with relevant AI actors and field data, and identification of incidents and errors, are identified and documented.

MANAGE.name: Manage
MANAGE.description: Risks are prioritized and acted upon based on a projected impact.

subcategories.MANAGE-1.1: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.
subcategories.MANAGE-1.2: Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.
subcategories.MANAGE-1.3: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority are developed, planned, and documented.
subcategories.MANAGE-1.4: Negative residual risks (to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and society) are documented.
subcategories.MANAGE-2.1: Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods.
subcategories.MANAGE-2.2: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.
subcategories.MANAGE-2.3: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
subcategories.MANAGE-2.4: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
subcategories.MANAGE-3.1: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored.
subcategories.MANAGE-3.2: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.
subcategories.MANAGE-4.1: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented.
subcategories.MANAGE-4.2: Measurable continuous improvement activities are integrated into AI system updates.
subcategories.MANAGE-4.3: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities.

genai_profile.name: NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile)
genai_profile.note: Companion profile for generative AI that maps unique risks to AI RMF subcategories. Incidents in this dataset prefer the core AI RMF subcategory identifiers above; the GenAI profile is supplemental context.
